Title and Author: AI-Powered MetaHuman Interviewer: Serious Game for Student Job Interview Skills (Kansada Mongkoljaturong, Mesa Manitsakulwong, Samart Moodleah - IEEE Access, Scopus Q1)
Technology Used: Photorealistic MetaHuman 3D avatar; Speech Recognition & Synthesis; NLP & LLM dialogue; Gamified performance scoring
Result: Successfully created an interactive digital interviewer that reduced candidate anxiety and measurably improved response structure and verbal self-efficacy.
Gap Identified: Relies on heavy 3D game engines (Unreal Engine/MetaHuman), making it impossible to run in a lightweight web browser; lacks live in-browser telemetry HUDs (real-time composure and vocal steadiness percentages).

Title and Author: MAG-BERT-ARL for Fair Automated Video Interview Assessment (Bagus Tris Atmaja, K. Azizah, Candy Olivia Mawalim, I. A. Hanif, Sakriani Sakti, Chee Wee Leong, Shogo Okada - IEEE Access, Scopus Q1)
Technology Used: Multimodal Adaptation Gate (MAG); BERT Language Representation; Adversarially Reweighted Learning (ARL); OpenFace & openSMILE
Result: Demonstrated that fusing facial movements, speech prosody, and verbal text achieves high predictive validity (r > 0.72) across automated interview competencies while reducing demographic bias.
Gap Identified: Designed strictly as an asynchronous employer-side screening filter rather than an interactive practice tool for candidates; does not provide conversational follow-up questions, coding sandboxes, or hints.

Title and Author: Prompting-in-a-Series: Psychology-Informed Contents and Embeddings for Personality Recognition with Decoder-Only Models (Jing Jie Tan, Ban-Hoe Kwan, Danny Wee-Kiat Ng, Yan-Chai Hum, Anissa Mokraoui, Shih-Yu Lo - IEEE Trans. on Comput. Social Systems, Scopus Q1)
Technology Used: Decoder-only LLMs (Llama / Mistral); PICEPR algorithm (Prompting-in-a-Series); Psychology-informed content embedding extractors
Result: Achieved a 5% to 15% performance improvement in soft-skill and personality trait recognition over baseline classifiers using modular prompting.
Gap Identified: Evaluates purely textual transcripts, completely lacking real-time audio prosody and facial computer-vision streams; operates as an offline post-hoc evaluation pipeline rather than a live interview interface.

Title and Author: Do We Need To Watch It All? Efficient Job Interview Video Processing with Differentiable Masking (Hung Le, Sixia Li, Candy Olivia Mawalim, Hung-Hsuan Huang, Chee Wee Leong, Shogo Okada - ACM ICMI, Scopus Indexed)
Technology Used: Differentiable Temporal Video Masking; Acoustic salient frame detection; Audio-Visual Transformer encoders
Result: Reduced processing time and compute requirements by 42% by selectively analyzing informative behavioral segments without sacrificing scoring accuracy.
Gap Identified: Geared towards server-side offline video batch evaluation; does not offer real-time in-session candidate feedback; does not support multi-round specialized tracks (Aptitude, DSA, System Design, HR).

Title and Author: Automated Interview Evaluation System Using RoBERTa Technology (S. S. Roy, et al. - IEEE Conference Series, Scopus Indexed)
Technology Used: RoBERTa transformer language model; Speech-to-Text conversion; Cosine similarity semantic scoring; Keyword and technical depth extraction
Result: Outperformed traditional TF-IDF and basic BERT models in evaluating technical correctness and linguistic coherence in spoken responses.
Gap Identified: Only evaluates the textual transcription, completely ignoring non-verbal delivery (posture, eye contact, speech steadiness); lacks an AI avatar interviewer and live candidate coaching.
